sections.html:
The office is at 112 W 2nd Street, Washington, NC 27889, with mail going to P.O. Box 514. Weekday hours are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., filings stop at 4:45 p.m., and the phone is 252-946-2323.

The registry handles deeds, deeds of trust, powers of attorney, plats, assumed business names, UCC statements, military discharges and vital records, and it administers notary oaths. Index, historical index and map searches run through beaufortcountyrod.com.

Under G.S. 84-4 and 84-5, staff cannot help prepare legal papers. Arrive with a finished deed from your lawyer.

sections.h2: What a Beaufort deed must show
sections.html:
State standards and local steps both apply.

  • Letter or legal paper, printed on one side in legible type of 9 points or larger on white stock.
  • Three blank inches at the head of page one, and half-inch margins elsewhere.
  • The kind of instrument written at the top of the first page.
  • A preparer's name on every deed and deed of trust.
  • On a deed, the buyer's address plus a note on whether the seller lived there as a primary residence.
  • A sign-off from Land Records on deeds and certain maps before filing.

Paper that misses the format rules can still be filed for a $25.00 nonstandard fee, and the register may waive that fee when only the type size is short and the text is legible. Surveys and plats, along with Torrens documents, cannot be filed electronically, so they go in on paper.

sections.h2: Why a deed goes through Land Records first
sections.html:
The county ties its mapping and tax listing to recorded deeds, so Land Records looks at a deed before the register files it. That office is at 220 N. Market Street in Washington, phone 252-946-6591.

Land Records manages the county's parcel mapping and GIS databases, applies recorded documents such as wills and deeds when it administers tax listings, and helps the public and professionals with record reviews. Drop the deed there early, since approval comes before recording.

The register's downloads also include a resolution on tax certification for deeds. Ask the register or the tax collector whether a certificate is needed for your closing, because the rule is set locally.

sections.h2: Costs to record in Beaufort County
sections.html:
State law (G.S. 161-10) fixes most amounts, and the register's guide adds the nonstandard charge.

Recording charges in Beaufort County
Document or serviceCharge
General instrument, such as a deed$26.00 up to 15 pages, then $4.00 a page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 up to 35 pages, then $4.00 a page
Release of a deed of trustNo fee
Plat$21.00 per sheet
Certified copy$5.00 for the first sheet, $2.00 for each more
Nonstandard document$25.00

Excise tax is a separate line. The seller pays a dollar per $500 of price at the registry, and the county retains half. For anything out of the ordinary, request the office's current schedule.

The registry emails you, at no charge, when a recorded document matches a name you enroll. Each email address can list five names, and only filings made after signup count.

The reason is simple: the office must record any document that is properly executed and presented with payment, and it cannot know whether a signature is forged. Nothing can be removed from the official records after recording, even if a document is proven fraudulent. An owner who suspects fraud should call the sheriff's office at 252-946-7111 and speak to an attorney, because the register has no power to reverse a filing.

The name you enroll can be your own or a relative's, which suits owners of land they rarely visit.

Beaufort is a coastal plain county built around the Pamlico River, with Washington, the county seat, where the Tar and Pamlico rivers meet. Seven municipalities lie within it: Aurora, Bath, Belhaven, Chocowinity, Pantego, Washington and Washington Park. Population is 44,670, and the county has 25,204 housing units with 69.5 percent of homes owner-occupied. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $192,700.

Waterfront and inland parcels do not move together. Property on or near the water has historically changed in value much faster than inland land, so the type of parcel matters more than the county average when you price a house.

sections.h2: How taxes interact with a sale
sections.html:
Bills are issued as of July 1 and fall due September 1. If payment is not in by January 5, interest and enforced collection start. For real estate, the owner on January 1 is the listing taxpayer and stays responsible until the past due date, whatever the buyer and seller agree at closing.

That is a trap for sellers. If you close after the bills go out, one may still arrive in your mail. Send it on to the buyer or return it to the collector. Escrow lenders are not automatic either: the owner must tell the lender the amount and confirm with the collector that payment arrived.

The 2025 revaluation took effect January 1, 2025, and a six-year cycle follows. Value appeals may be filed from January each year, up to the adjournment of the county review board, typically in mid-April. County, fire and EMS district rates are set with the county budget, while town officials set municipal rates. Vehicles are taxed through the NCDMV at tag renewal, not on the real estate bill. The tax collector offers payment plans with a 20 percent down payment, set up in person between January 6 and June 30.

sections.h2: Getting ready to file your deed
sections.html:
Work through the order of the visit. First, have your lawyer finish the deed with the preparer's name, the buyer's address and the residence note. Second, take it to Land Records at 220 N. Market Street for sign-off, and ask whether a tax certificate is needed. Third, bring the deed and the fees to the registry before 4:45 p.m. Fourth, pay the excise tax, since the seller owes it at the registry. Afterward, make sure the tax bill reaches the right person, and consider signing up for the fraud alert on your name.

After recording, you can confirm the deed through the index search at beaufortcountyrod.com. If you need proof for a lender or an attorney, a certified copy costs $5.00 for the first sheet and $2.00 for each more. Keep the recorded copy with your closing papers. If the release of your old deed of trust has not shown up in the index, ask the lender, since that release records at no fee.

faqs.q: When is the last filing time in Beaufort County?
faqs.a: Filing closes at 4:45 p.m., fifteen minutes before the 5 p.m. weekday close. The office is at 112 W 2nd Street in Washington and can be reached at 252-946-2323.

faqs.q: Does a deed need Land Records approval in Beaufort County?
faqs.a: Yes. Deeds and some maps must be approved by the Beaufort County Land Records office before recording. Land Records is at 220 N. Market Street, phone 252-946-6591.

faqs.q: Can I record a plat electronically in Beaufort County?
faqs.a: No. Survey maps and plats, along with Torrens documents, are not accepted electronically. Those are the only document types excluded from electronic recording.

faqs.q: Who pays the tax bill after a Beaufort sale?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner stays responsible until the past due date, regardless of what the buyer and seller arranged at closing. Send any notice to the buyer or back to the collector.

faqs.q: Can Beaufort County warn me about filings in my name?
faqs.a: Yes. The register runs a free fraud alert email service. You can enroll five names per email address and receive a notice when a matching document is recorded, but only for documents recorded after signup.
